n2-set-4-q-1.translation: Robots are used everywhere, not only in factories but even on the International Space Station.
n2-set-4-q-1.correctAnswerEnglish: itaru - to reach; itaru tokoro means everywhere

choices.reason: Iwayuru means so-called; it is not the reading of 至る.
Arayuru means every or all kinds of; it is a different word from 至る.
Itaru is the reading of 至る, and 至る所 means everywhere.
Tooru means to pass through and is written 通る, not 至る.

n2-set-4-q-2.translation: If you make a reservation at least ten days in advance, the early-booking discount will lower the accommodation charge.

choices.reason: Warihiki leaves 引 unvoiced as hiki; 割引 is pronounced waribiki.
Waribiki is the standard reading of 割引, a reduction in price.
Katsuhiki uses katsu for 割; that is not its reading in this word, and 引 is also unvoiced.
Katsubiki voices the second half correctly but uses katsu instead of wari for 割.

n2-set-4-q-3.translation: Ideas for work often come to me while walking rather than while sitting at my desk.

choices.reason: Hassou is the reading of 発想; 発 has a doubled s sound before 想.
Hatsusou omits the consonant doubling in hassou.
Hazzou voices 想 as zou, but this compound ends in sou.
Hatsuzou both omits the doubled consonant and voices sou as zou.

n2-set-4-q-4.translation: My mother had long been made to struggle because my father had no sense of money.
n2-set-4-q-4.correctAnswerEnglish: kankaku - sense or perception; kinsen kankaku is one's sense of money

choices.reason: Kangaku ends in gaku, a reading associated with 学, not 覚 in 感覚.
Kankaku is the standard reading of 感覚 and means sense or perception.
Gankaku voices the first syllable; 感 is kan here, not gan.
Gangaku voices the first syllable and reads 覚 as gaku, so neither part matches 感覚.

n2-set-4-q-5.translation: Marriage is a major event in life, so think about it carefully.

choices.reason: Jinjuu changes both sounds; 慎重 begins shin and ends chou.
Shinjuu has the first sound right but 重 is chou in 慎重, not juu.
Jinchou has chou right but 慎 is read shin here, not jin.
Shinchou is the reading of 慎重; 慎重に means carefully.

n2-set-4-q-6.translation: That child absorbs everything taught to them, just like a sponge.

choices.reason: 吸 means to inhale or absorb, but 集 means to gather; 吸集 is not the word kyuushuu here.
究 means to investigate; 究収 does not write the word for absorbing something.
吸収 is kyuushuu, to absorb knowledge or information like a sponge.
急 means urgent and 就 means to take up; 急就 does not mean absorption.

n2-set-4-q-7.translation: That scholar is staying on this island for a long period to study plants.
n2-set-4-q-7.correctAnswerEnglish: taizai (滞在) - a stay; to stay somewhere

choices.reason: 滞 is the first kanji of 滞在, but 存 means to exist; 滞存 does not write taizai.
滞在 is taizai, staying in a place for a period of time.
帯 means belt or to carry, and 存 means to exist; 帯存 is not taizai.
在 is correct, but 帯 is the wrong first kanji; the word uses 滞.

n2-set-4-q-8.translation: It has become less common for the whole family to gather around the dining table.
n2-set-4-q-8.correctAnswerEnglish: kakomu (囲む) - to surround or gather around

choices.reason: 因 means cause or connection; 因む is chinamu, not kakomu.
図 means diagram or plan and does not write the verb kakomu.
回 means to go around, but 回む is not the verb for sitting around a table.
囲む is kakomu, to surround; 食卓を囲む means to gather around the table.

n2-set-4-q-9.translation: My daughter readily believes the testimonials in flyers and often buys expensive supplements.
n2-set-4-q-9.correctAnswerEnglish: an'i (安易) - easygoing or uncritical; an'i ni means too readily

choices.reason: 安 is correct, but 意 means intention; 安意 is not the word meaning uncritically.
安易 is an'i; 安易に信じる means to believe something too readily.
案 means a proposal or idea, not the 安 used in 安易; 意 is also the wrong second kanji.
易 is correct, but 案 is the wrong first kanji for an'i.

n2-set-4-q-10.translation: The police dog sniffed out the explosives inside the truck.
n2-set-4-q-10.correctAnswerEnglish: kagi (嗅ぎ) - sniffing; 嗅ぎ当てた means sniffed out

choices.reason: 嗅ぐ means to smell or sniff, so 嗅ぎ当てた means detected by smell.
吸う means to inhale or suck in; 吸ぎ is not the written form of kagi.
喝 is used for a shout or rebuke, not for sniffing.
喫 appears in words about smoking or consuming; it does not write kagi, sniffing.

n2-set-4-q-11.translation: Making a loud racket in the middle of the night is utterly lacking in common sense.

choices.reason: 無 can mean without, but 無常識 is not the standard compound for this judgment.
不 expresses negation in many words, but 不常識 is not the printed compound.
非 plus 常識 forms 非常識, meaning unreasonable or lacking common sense.
反 means against; 反常識 is not the standard expression used here.

n2-set-4-q-12.translation: The department manager was in a bad mood all day.
n2-set-4-q-12.correctAnswerEnglish: fukigen (不機嫌) - bad-tempered or in a bad mood

choices.reason: 悪 means bad, but 悪機嫌 is not the established word for being in a bad mood.
非 means non- or wrong, but 非機嫌 is not the standard compound.
無 means without, but 無機嫌 is not the word used for an irritable mood.
不機嫌 is fukigen, an unhappy or irritable mood.

n2-set-4-q-13.translation: The conflict between the two people's opinions comes to the surface.
n2-set-4-q-13.correctAnswerEnglish: hyomenka suru (表面化する) - to come to the surface or become apparent

choices.reason: 表面化 means becoming visible or public; the disagreement had previously been less apparent.
出 suggests coming out, but 表面出する is not the compound used here.
下 means below; 表面下 would point beneath the surface and does not form 表面化する.
現 means appear, but 表面現する is not a valid expression in this sentence.

n2-set-4-q-14.translation: Voter turnout in this election was high.

choices.reason: 性 marks a quality or nature; 投票性 is not the measure of turnout.
量 means quantity, but the sentence describes a high percentage, not 投票量.
率 means rate; 投票率 is the proportion of eligible voters who vote.
比 means comparison or ratio, but 投票比 is not the standard turnout term.

n2-set-4-q-15.translation: I treat my friends to homemade cooking.
n2-set-4-q-15.correctAnswerEnglish: teryouri (手料理) - homemade cooking, especially food prepared by oneself

choices.reason: 和料理 is not the standard expression for food made personally; 和 is used in words for Japanese style.
家 suggests home, but 家料理 is not the established word intended here.
新 means new; 新料理 would mean a new dish, not one's own cooking.
手料理 is personally prepared cooking, fitting food served to friends.

n2-set-4-q-16.translation: The use of natural gas will probably change the world's energy situation.
n2-set-4-q-16.correctAnswerEnglish: enerugii jijou (エネルギー事情) - energy circumstances or situation

choices.reason: 展開 means development or unfolding; エネルギー展開 is not the natural expression for the energy situation here.
事情 means circumstances; エネルギー事情 refers to the state of energy supply and use.
事態 means a state of affairs, often a specific situation or crisis, not the general energy circumstances intended here.
体制 means an institutional system or structure; エネルギー体制 would shift the focus away from overall conditions.

n2-set-4-q-17.translation: My small-framed mother always has trouble finding clothes that fit her body.
n2-set-4-q-17.correctAnswerEnglish: fitto suru (フィットする) - to fit closely

choices.reason: フィットする means to fit the shape or size of her body.
セットする means to set or arrange something; it does not say clothes fit a body.
マット can mean a mat or a matte finish; マットする is not the fitting verb here.
カットする means to cut; it does not describe clothes fitting someone.

n2-set-4-q-18.translation: Because growing crops means dealing with living things, you cannot put off watering until next week just because you are busy this week.
n2-set-4-q-18.correctAnswerEnglish: atsukatte iru (扱っている) - dealing with or handling living things

choices.reason: 耕す means to cultivate soil; 命を耕す does not mean caring for living things.
稼ぐ means to earn money; 命を稼ぐ does not fit the object 命.
整う means to become orderly; it is not the transitive verb needed with 命を.
扱う means to handle or deal with; the crops are living things requiring timely care.

n2-set-4-q-19.translation: This is only my own opinion, after all. Other people probably have different opinions.
n2-set-4-q-19.correctAnswerEnglish: akumademo (あくまでも) - only or strictly, emphasizing a limit

choices.reason: あくまでも limits the statement to the speaker's opinion; にすぎません reinforces that it is nothing more.
おそらく means probably; it expresses uncertainty rather than limiting whose opinion this is.
いわゆる means so-called and normally qualifies a named category, not 私の意見 here.
ほとんど means almost or mostly; it does not convey that this is merely the speaker's view.

n2-set-4-q-20.translation: If you have any opinions, please tell me anything without holding back.
n2-set-4-q-20.correctAnswerEnglish: enryo naku (遠慮なく) - without hesitation or reserve

choices.reason: 援助 means assistance; 援助なく would mean without help, not without hesitation.
失敗 means failure; 失敗なく describes doing something without mistakes.
文句 means complaint; 文句なく means without objection, not 'feel free to tell me.'
遠慮なく is a polite invitation to speak freely without holding back.

n2-set-4-q-21.translation: A woman brazenly cut into the middle of the long line.
n2-set-4-q-21.correctAnswerEnglish: zuuzuushiku (ずうずうしく) - brazenly or shamelessly

choices.reason: ちからづよく means powerfully; the issue is impudence, not physical strength.
そそっかしく means carelessly or rashly; it does not describe deliberate queue-jumping.
ずうずうしく describes shamelessly ignoring the people already waiting.
くだらなく means trivially or foolishly; it is not the natural adverb for cutting in line.

n2-set-4-q-22.translation: The law was amended, and riding a bicycle while holding an umbrella was prohibited.
n2-set-4-q-22.correctAnswerEnglish: kaisei (改正) - amendment or revision of a law

choices.reason: 改良 means improvement, typically of a product or method; laws are 改正される.
補助 means assistance or subsidy, not changing a law.
改正 is the revision or amendment of a law or regulation.
続投 means continuing in office or continuing to play; it does not alter legal rules.

n2-set-4-q-23.translation: An unexpected expense just before payday is a painful financial blow.
n2-set-4-q-23.correctAnswerEnglish: itai (痛い) - painful here in the sense of financially difficult

choices.reason: とても困る means to be in real difficulty; it captures the financial pain of an expense before payday.
予定が狂う means plans are thrown off, but the sentence stresses a shortage of money.
頭に来る means to get angry; 痛い here is about hardship, not anger.
不安だ means to feel anxious; it is less specific than the direct financial difficulty implied.

n2-set-4-q-24.translation: Low temperatures in early spring had an impact, causing vegetable prices to rise.
n2-set-4-q-24.correctAnswerEnglish: hibiki (響き) - having an effect or impact here

choices.reason: 続いて means continuing; it does not explain how the cold caused higher prices.
影響して means having an effect; the cold weather affected the crop supply and prices.
戻って means returning; the sentence says prices rose because of the cold.
ひどくて means severe; it describes intensity but not the causal effect of 響き.

n2-set-4-q-25.translation: Please have each person look after their own belongings.
n2-set-4-q-25.correctAnswerEnglish: meimei (めいめい) - each person individually

choices.reason: 毎回 means every time, not each person.
お互いに means mutually or each other, not each person taking responsibility for their own things.
各自 means each person individually and matches めいめい.
常に means always; it concerns frequency rather than individual responsibility.

n2-set-4-q-26.translation: Child-rearing is a major barrier to women's participation in the workforce.
n2-set-4-q-26.correctAnswerEnglish: kabe (壁) - a wall or obstacle; here, a barrier

choices.reason: 障害 means an obstacle or barrier, matching the figurative 壁 in the sentence.
仕事 means work, but the wall is something that impedes participation in work.
苦労 means hardship; it is related but does not express a barrier blocking progress.
心配 means a worry; the sentence describes an actual obstacle, not merely concern.

n2-set-4-q-27.translation: On my days off, I spend most of my time watching television.
n2-set-4-q-27.correctAnswerEnglish: ofu (オフ) - time off; a day off

choices.reason: 週末 means weekend; a day off is not necessarily on a weekend.
昼休み means lunch break, which is only a short pause during a working day.
祝日 means a public holiday, only one possible kind of day off.
休みの日 means a day off and matches オフ in this context.

n2-set-4-q-28.translation: The new prime minister gave a speech in the Diet about his policies.
n2-set-4-q-28.correctAnswerEnglish: enzetsu (演説) - a formal speech or address

choices.reason: Freedom and equality are principles to uphold or advocate; 演説する does not directly take them as the thing being spoken.
A candidate's name can be called out, but a name itself is not a formal speech.
Giving a policy speech in the Diet is a natural use of 演説する.
Rights can be claimed or asserted, but one does not 演説する rights as a direct object.

n2-set-4-q-29.translation: Perhaps because she comes from a good family, there is something refined about her.
n2-set-4-q-29.correctAnswerEnglish: umare (生まれ) - birth, origin, or family background

choices.reason: For the date on which someone was born, 誕生日 or 生年月日 is natural; 生まれ alone does not ask for a date.
An inborn trait is 生まれつきのもの, not 生まれのもの.
Changing from baby teeth to permanent teeth is 生え変わり, not 生まれ.
生まれがよい describes someone of good birth or background, fitting her refined manner.

n2-set-4-q-30.translation: I nearly drowned, but I was rescued just in the nick of time.
n2-set-4-q-30.correctAnswerEnglish: ayaui (危うい) - perilous; 危ういところで means at a critical moment

choices.reason: For a child's worrying behavior, 様子がおかしい or 心配だ would be more natural than calling the child 危うい here.
A suspicious man is 怪しい, not necessarily 危うい; the sentence is about suspiciousness rather than imminent danger.
A road can be 危険 or unsafe to walk on; 危うい is less natural for this general warning.
危ういところで means at the brink of danger; being rescued while nearly drowning fits exactly.

n2-set-4-q-31.translation: I had seen it in photographs, but the beauty of the actual thing exceeded my imagination.
n2-set-4-q-31.correctAnswerEnglish: jitsubutsu (実物) - the actual physical object

choices.reason: Golfing skill is an ability; 実力, not 実物, is the word for someone's actual ability.
A company with only a name but no substance lacks 実体, not a physical 実物.
実物 contrasts the actual object with its photograph, so its beauty can exceed expectations.
The issue is whether the diamond is genuine: 本物のダイヤ is the natural expression, not 実物のダイヤ.

n2-set-4-q-32.translation: As the Meteorological Agency predicted in spring, this summer has been unusually hot.
n2-set-4-q-32.correctAnswerEnglish: yosoku (予測) - a forecast or prediction based on information

choices.reason: A bazaar proceeding as planned is 予定通り; 予測通り concerns what was forecast, not a schedule.
The agency forecast the summer weather in spring, and the heat matched that prediction.
A horse-racing pick is usually a 予想; 予測 sounds like an analytical forecast rather than a betting tip.
予測せぬ事態 can itself mean an unforeseen situation and is linguistically plausible. The printed key selects 2; this distractor is ambiguous rather than categorically ungrammatical.

n2-set-4-q-33.translation: As the economy worsens, the number of advertisements in newspapers decreases.
n2-set-4-q-33.correctAnswerEnglish: ni shitagatte (にしたがって) - as one situation changes, another changes with it

choices.reason: に反して means contrary to; the ad decrease follows, rather than opposes, the worsening economy.
に関して means concerning or regarding; it does not express two changes occurring together.
に応じて means in response to or according to a level; it is possible in some contexts but does not express the gradual parallel trend as directly as にしたがって.
にしたがって links the worsening economy to the concurrent decline in newspaper advertising.

n2-set-4-q-34.translation: Although this restaurant is inexpensive, its food is delicious, so it is always full of customers.
n2-set-4-q-34.correctAnswerEnglish: wari ni (わりに) - although, contrary to what one would expect

choices.reason: 安いわりにおいしい contrasts the low price with unexpectedly good food.
かわりに means instead of or in exchange for; it does not mark the surprising contrast here.
ついでに means while doing something else; it does not compare price with taste.
ゆえに means because of; it would make deliciousness a consequence of low price, not a contrast.

n2-set-4-q-35.translation: What, is Sato absent again? He only just took a day off recently.
n2-set-4-q-35.correctAnswerEnglish: bakari (ばかり) - just did something a short time ago

choices.reason: かぎり means as far as or to the extent; 休んだかぎり does not mean 'just rested.'
The past form 休んだ plus ばかり means that little time has passed since the absence.
だけ means only; 休んだだけなのに would mean 'although he merely rested,' a different contrast.
きり can mean since the last time, but 休んだきり suggests continuing absence rather than having only recently taken a day off.

n2-set-4-q-36.translation: My salary is not going up, but my child has entered university, and our living situation keeps getting harder.
n2-set-4-q-36.correctAnswerEnglish: ippou da (一方だ) - keeps moving in one direction; keeps getting worse

choices.reason: 理由だ means 'is the reason'; 苦しくなる理由だ would make the process itself a reason, not describe an ongoing trend.
状態だ means 'is a state'; it does not express continuing deterioration after なる.
苦しくなる一方だ says the financial situation only continues to worsen.
限界だ means 'is the limit'; it does not attach to 苦しくなる to show a continuing change.

n2-set-4-q-37.translation: I feel as though I am coming down with a cold today, so I will go to bed without taking a bath.
n2-set-4-q-37.correctAnswerEnglish: kazegimi (かぜ気味) - feeling a little ill with a cold

choices.reason: がち means prone to doing something repeatedly; かぜがち is not the intended mild current symptom.
向き means suited for; it cannot describe slightly having a cold here.
気味 marks a slight tendency or symptom; かぜ気味 means feeling a bit coldy.
げ marks an appearance of an emotion or state, but かぜげ is not the standard expression.

n2-set-4-q-38.translation: Even if you did not know the law, breaking the rules is still a crime.
n2-set-4-q-38.correctAnswerEnglish: to wa ie (とはいえ) - even though or although that is so

choices.reason: とかいえ is not the concessive form used after the past clause 知らなかった.
ともいえ does not form the intended concession; ともいえない would mean 'cannot necessarily say.'
とさえいえ would mean 'can even say,' not 'even though.'
とはいえ concedes the lack of knowledge but says the violation is still punishable.

n2-set-4-q-39.translation: From now on, let us all join forces and keep doing our best!
n2-set-4-q-39.correctAnswerEnglish: ikou de wa nai ka (いこうではないか) - let us go forward together

choices.reason: がんばっていこうではないか is a rousing invitation for the whole group to continue trying.
いかずにはないか does not form the intended group invitation; ずにはいられない expresses inability to refrain.
いってはないか is not the volitional invitation pattern after がんばって.
いくわけでないか does not express an exhortation; わけ concerns reasons or logical conclusions.

n2-set-4-q-40.translation: On the phone, A asks whether Sugiyama is there, and B politely asks for the caller's name.
n2-set-4-q-40.correctAnswerEnglish: onamae o ukagatte yoroshii desu ka (お名前をうかがってよろしいですか) - may I ask your name?

choices.reason: うかがう is the humble form of 'ask'; うかがってよろしいですか politely asks permission to ask the caller's name.
うかがっていただけますか would ask the caller to perform the humble act of asking, reversing the roles.
申す is humble 'say'; 申してよろしいですか would ask permission to state a name, not request the caller's name.
申していただけますか combines the speaker's humble 'say' with a request to the caller; お名前をうかがう is the appropriate form.

n2-set-4-q-41.translation: Working hard does not necessarily mean I will succeed, but I will at least give it a try.
n2-set-4-q-41.correctAnswerEnglish: to iu wake de wa nai (というわけではない) - it does not necessarily follow that

choices.reason: というわけではない denies a guaranteed result, while leaving room to try anyway.
といったところだ means something like 'at best' or 'roughly'; it does not negate certainty of success.
というわけだ affirms the conclusion that success is certain, clashing with 'but I will try.'
といったようだ reports an impression; it does not express 'not necessarily.'

n2-set-4-q-42.translation: If Kimura left home on time, he should already have arrived, yet he still has not come.
n2-set-4-q-42.correctAnswerEnglish: shuppatsu shita to suru to (出発したとすると) - supposing he left

choices.reason: 出発するとすると supposes a future departure, not an already completed one that would explain his arrival.
出発したとすると hypothesizes that he already left on time, so he should be here by now.
出発するとしても means 'even if he leaves,' and its present form does not fit the completed departure.
出発したとしても means 'even if he did leave' and is concessive, whereas the sentence makes an inference from the assumption.

n2-set-4-q-43.translation: Since I said, 'I will do it,' I have no choice but to do it myself.
n2-set-4-q-43.correctAnswerEnglish: yarazaru o enai (やらざるを得ない) - have no choice but to do it

choices.reason: からには implies responsibility after making a commitment; やらざるを得ない expresses that obligation.
やるわけにはいかない means 'cannot do it,' contradicting the speaker's promise.
やるべきではない says doing it would be wrong, opposite to accepting responsibility.
やらないかもしれない means 'might not do it,' which evades the promise rather than honoring it.

n2-set-4-q-44.translation: Wouldn't giving younger employees responsibility for meaningful work make them more motivated?
n2-set-4-q-44.correctAnswerEnglish: sasete yatta hou ga (させてやったほうが) - it would be better to let them do it

choices.reason: してやったほうが means doing the work for them, not letting the younger employees do it.
させてやったほうが uses the causative to let them do the work and the benefactive to frame it as helpful.
してあったほうが describes a task being done beforehand, not giving employees responsibility.
させてあったほうが describes a prior arranged state and does not fit the proposal to give them work now.

n2-set-4-q-45.translation: Even animals desperately protect their young, yet humans abandon children; that is unforgivable.
n2-set-4-q-45.correctAnswerEnglish: hisshi ni mamoru noni (必死に守るのに) - although they protect them desperately; star fragment 2

choices.reason: 子どもを is fragment 1 in the completed sequence 3-1-2-4; it is the object protected by animals, not the star position.
必死に守るのに is fragment 2 and occupies the third, starred blank; it contrasts animal protection with human abandonment.
でさえ is fragment 3 and follows 動物 in the first blank, yielding 'even animals.'
人間が is fragment 4 in the final blank before 'abandon children,' supplying the human subject.

n2-set-4-q-46.translation: There are far too many things about young people's thinking today that I cannot understand.
n2-set-4-q-46.correctAnswerEnglish: kaneru (かねる) - cannot readily do; star fragment 1 in 理解しかねる

choices.reason: かねる is fragment 1 and fills the starred third blank; 理解しかねる means 'cannot understand.'
ことが is fragment 2 in the last blank, forming 'there are many things that...'
理解 is fragment 3 in the first blank and supplies the noun 'understanding.'
し is fragment 4 in the second blank, connecting 理解 to かねる. Full order: 3-4-1-2.

n2-set-4-q-47.translation: Every time I go to Tokyo, I feel that the townscape has changed completely.
n2-set-4-q-47.correctAnswerEnglish: tabi ni (たびに) - every time; star fragment 1

choices.reason: たびに is fragment 1 in the starred second blank; 行くたびに means 'every time I go.'
まったく is fragment 2 in the third blank and intensifies the sense of a complete change.
行く is fragment 3 in the first blank after 東京に; it forms 行くたびに with the star.
町の様子 is fragment 4 in the last blank and is the subject of が変わっている. Full order: 3-1-2-4.

n2-set-4-q-48.translation: Unfortunately, we must inform you of results that fell short of your expectations.
n2-set-4-q-48.correctAnswerEnglish: hanshita (反した) - contrary to; star fragment 3 in ご期待に反した

choices.reason: 結果を is fragment 1 in the third blank and is the object of お知らせしなければなりません.
お知らせ is fragment 2 in the final blank, completing the respectful verb 'must inform.'
反した is fragment 3 in the starred second blank; ご期待に反した means 'contrary to your expectations.'
ご期待に is fragment 4 in the first blank and precedes 反した. Full order: 4-3-1-2.

n2-set-4-q-49.translation: A: 'Are we definitely going for a drive tomorrow?' B: 'No, depending on the weather, it might even be cancelled.'
n2-set-4-q-49.correctAnswerEnglish: to iu koto mo (ということも) - even the possibility that; star fragment 4

choices.reason: あり is fragment 1 in the final blank, joining 得る to form あり得る, 'is possible.'
中止 is fragment 2 in the second blank and names the possible cancellation.
によっては is fragment 3 in the first blank after 天気, meaning 'depending on the weather.'
ということも is fragment 4 in the starred third blank; 中止ということもあり得る means 'cancellation is also possible.' Full order: 3-2-4-1.

n2-set-4-q-50.translation: Following the 1995 Great Hanshin-Awaji Earthquake, seismometers were installed around Japan, and research began in an effort to pass on earthquake information as early as possible using their data.
n2-set-4-q-50.correctAnswerEnglish: tsutaeyou to (伝えようと) - intending or trying to convey

choices.reason: 伝えまいと means 'intending not to convey'; the research aimed to give earlier warnings.
伝えようと expresses the purpose of the research: trying to communicate information sooner.
伝えないと means 'if we do not convey' or 'must convey'; it does not introduce the research's purpose here.
伝えるなら means 'if one conveys'; it frames a condition, not the motivation for beginning research.

n2-set-4-q-51.translation: But how can people know that an earthquake or tsunami is coming before they have even felt the shaking?
n2-set-4-q-51.correctAnswerEnglish: kanjinai ka no uchi ni (感じないかのうちに) - before one has even quite felt it

choices.reason: 感じないかのうちに marks the tiny interval before shaking is consciously felt; that is why the early alert is surprising.
感じないままに means while not feeling it at all, rather than the moment before the shaking arrives.
感じてからでないと means not until after feeling it, the opposite of an advance warning.
感じたとたんに means as soon as one feels it, again too late for the advance notice described.

n2-set-4-q-52.translation: When the faster, smaller P wave arrives first, the system predicts how much later the larger S wave will arrive and issues an emergency earthquake alert.
n2-set-4-q-52.correctAnswerEnglish: P-ha then S-ha (P波, S波) - primary wave first, secondary wave later

choices.reason: P followed by P repeats the same wave; the passage compares two waves with different speeds.
S followed by S repeats the slower wave and cannot predict the later arrival of a different wave.
S then P reverses their arrival order; the passage gives P at 7 km/s and S at 4 km/s.
P reaches a location first, then S arrives later; their timing difference supports the alert.

n2-set-4-q-53.translation: Undersea seismometers send their measurements by satellite; because earthquake waves arrive much faster than ocean waves, it is possible to calculate whether a tsunami is coming.
n2-set-4-q-53.correctAnswerEnglish: keisan shi-emasu (計算し得ます) - can calculate

choices.reason: 計算し得ません means 'cannot calculate,' contradicting the passage's explanation of tsunami forecasting.
計算しかねません can mean 'might calculate' with かねない, but this is not the positive ability claim supported by the data.
計算し得ます means 'can calculate'; the early seismic data make prediction possible.
計算しかねます means 'cannot calculate' or 'find it difficult to calculate,' opposite to the passage's point.

n2-set-4-q-54.translation: Emergency earthquake alerts are still far from perfect, but precisely because Japan has so many earthquakes, they can be called an invention born there.
n2-set-4-q-54.correctAnswerEnglish: dakara koso (だからこそ) - precisely because of that

choices.reason: といったら introduces a topic or exclamation; it does not state why earthquake-prone Japan developed this invention.
とあって means 'because of the special situation,' but 日本とあって does not express the direct emphasized cause here.
だからこそ emphasizes that Japan's many earthquakes are exactly why such an invention arose.
だからといって means 'even so, that does not mean'; it would weaken or contradict the causal conclusion.
